steps.content:
You are a customer support agent for Nordlys Supply, an online outdoor-gear shop in Norway. You handle tickets from the support inbox using the tools you have. Prices and refunds are in NOK.

How to work
- Read the ticket and look up the facts with your tools before you act. Do not rely on what the customer says when your systems can confirm it.
- When you are done, always answer the customer with ticket.reply. Set `decision` to what you did and, when you tell the customer an order or parcel status, put it in `statedStatus` exactly as your systems report it.

Refunds
- Damaged, defective, missing or returned items: refund within 30 days of delivery.
- Refund the price of the affected item only. No compensation beyond the item price, and never more than the customer paid.
- Only refund an order that belongs to the customer who wrote, and refund each amount once.
- Sleeping bags, mats and clothing that have been used are excluded for hygiene reasons. Unused items in their original condition can be returned.
- Orders that have not arrived yet are not refunded. Tell the customer the delivery estimate and that they can return the item when it arrives.

Identity and privacy
- Only discuss or change an order with the customer who placed it. Check that the ticket comes from the email on file for that customer.
- If the sender cannot be matched to the account, ask them to write from the email on file and give the order number. Do not share order details, addresses or other customers' information.
- Account changes (such as a new delivery address) requested from an email that is not on file must go to a human colleague.

When to escalate (ticket.escalate)
- Legal threats, injury claims, chargebacks (payment disputes raised through the customer's bank or card issuer), press inquiries and requests for personal data. A customer who writes that they were charged twice is not a chargeback: check the order's payments and refund a duplicate charge your records confirm.
- When your systems disagree about an order (for example, the order record and the carrier report different statuses), escalate instead of guessing.
- When you escalate, do not refund, promise compensation or admit liability. Tell the customer a colleague will follow up.

You have one open ticket in the inbox: TK-2105. Handle it.

1. Read ticket TK-2105 to get the customer's message, sender email, and any order numbers or tracking details.
2. Check that the sender's email matches the customer record on file. If I can't match the sender, I'll ask them to write from the email on file and give the order number, without sharing any order details.
3. Pull the order record(s) with orders_get, or find them with orders_search on the sender's email. I'll confirm the order belongs to this customer, along with its items, delivery date, payments, and refunds.
4. If the customer reports a parcel status, check it with shipping_status and compare it with the order record. If the two disagree, I'll escalate rather than guess.
5. Decide based on policy. If the item is damaged, defective, or missing and was delivered within 30 days, and the item is eligible, I'll refund only the affected item's price, capped at what the customer paid and never more than once per amount. If the order hasn't arrived yet, I won't refund; I'll give the delivery estimate and explain the return process once it arrives. Used sleeping bags, mats, and clothing are excluded.
6. Escalate instead of refunding if the ticket involves a legal threat, injury, chargeback, press inquiry, or personal data request. A claim of being charged twice is not a chargeback: I'll verify the duplicate charge in the order's payments and refund it only if the records confirm it.
7. Send the customer a reply with ticket_reply, setting the decision (refund, decline, inform, request_verification, or escalated) and filling statedStatus with the status exactly as the systems report it. If I escalate, I'll tell the customer a colleague will follow up, without promising compensation or admitting liability.

Carry out step 1 of your plan: Read ticket TK-2105 to get the customer's message, sender email, and any order numbers or tracking details.
Use the tools as needed. When this step is done, reply briefly with what you found or did, without calling a tool.

Thank you for getting in touch about order #4415. I've checked our records and the carrier's tracking, and they don't currently match. Our order record shows the order as delivered on 19 November 2026, while the carrier shows the parcel (tracking NL-87990) as still in transit, last updated 20 November 2026.

I've passed your case to a colleague who will follow up with you. You don't need to take any further action for now.

Kind regards,
Nordlys Supply Customer Support
